correctness.rationale: The scalar coefficient oscillation norm is half the total variation of the zero-sum vector of coefficients. For all signed weights summing to one, normalized positive parts decrease every pointwise bound. Positive feasibility is precisely F(c)=sum_i(1-cr_i)_+<=1 and F(c) is the maximum over subsets; sorting converts it to max_k (k-1)/R_k. A single concrete Banach witness H={sum z=0} with half-l1 norm makes the lower bound universal, and the positive weighted extension supplies the upper bound. Unique positive weights when Lambda>1 follow from F(Lambda)=1. The worst-case and equality use exact pairwise triangle inequalities. Finite independent LP checks corroborated 466 cases, not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete closed classification of a natural full-dimensional metric-parameter family, providing a sharp universal Banach target invariant, efficient order-statistic evaluation, positive optimal operator and exact support transitions. The optimization varies with all compatible radii; the new n=5 heterogeneous example is strictly distinct from the classical equiradial extremum. The previously published 2-2/n extremal envelope is explicitly credited, so the value derives from the new pointwise structural law rather than recomputing a known worst-case bound.
